decisions.title: Strict Pydantic contracts are the compiler boundary
decisions.decision: All pipeline artifacts are represented as strict Pydantic models with unknown fields forbidden and explicit rationale fields.
consequences: LLM structured outputs can be validated before entering later stages.
Tests can assert deterministic JSON contracts without executing LLM calls.
decisions.rationale: The compiler must reject malformed artifacts early and make every generated decision auditable.

decisions.title: Compiler stages are independently testable
decisions.decision: Stage contracts and execution logs are module-level primitives with no shared mutable pipeline state.
consequences: Each future phase can add tests for its own stage without requiring a full pipeline run.
Targeted repair can operate on one layer without regenerating unrelated artifacts.
decisions.rationale: Independent testing and repair are required for deterministic production behavior.

decisions.title: Execution logs are JSON artifacts
decisions.decision: Every stage log uses a strict StageExecutionLog model and is written as JSON under logs.
consequences: Pipeline runs are observable and machine-readable.
Evaluation can aggregate latency, validation failures, repair attempts, and status.
decisions.rationale: Compiler behavior must be measurable across validation, repair, and runtime generation stages.

decisions.title: Phase 2 uses deterministic structured planners
decisions.decision: Intent extraction and architecture planning are implemented as deterministic functions that return strict Pydantic models, with no free-form pipeline output.
consequences: Phase 2 behavior is reproducible in tests without relying on model availability or sampling controls.
Future Instructor or PydanticAI adapters can be added behind the same IntentIR and ArchitectureManifest contracts.
decisions.rationale: The compiler must prioritize reliability, validation, and temperature-zero execution before introducing LLM orchestration.

decisions.title: Architecture manifests are traceable and schema-generator ready
decisions.decision: Architecture elements carry source_intent_fields, pages reference existing flows, roles require permissions, business rules reference existing roles or entities, and integrations expose API-oriented capabilities.
consequences: Phase 3 schema generators can consume ArchitectureManifest without reparsing natural language.
Future validators can detect missing role permissions, page-flow gaps, invalid business rule references, and integration mapping defects.
decisions.rationale: The ArchitectureManifest must be a deterministic bridge from IntentIR to schema generation, not a loose descriptive document.

decisions.title: Phase 3 schema generators are isolated contract compilers
decisions.decision: UI, API, database, and auth schemas are generated by independent modules that consume ArchitectureManifest and AppSpec and return strict Pydantic schema models.
consequences: Each schema layer can be regenerated and tested independently.
Later validation and repair phases can compare strict schema contracts without reparsing natural language.
decisions.rationale: Independent schema generation reduces shared mutable state and makes targeted repair possible in later phases.
